A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same BoostCD/BoostIE study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H can be matched despite relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original BoostIE experiments on Wiki-cIE Code, human evaluation on Wikipedia text, and error analyses in Tables 1–3 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds a quantitative comparison of constrained and unconstrained SynthIE errors in Appendix H.1, Table 4.

M1.justification: Sections 2–3 retain the same constrained/unconstrained base-model passes, boosted model, entity-removal training procedure, and DPO finetuning. The expanded training-data explanation does not change the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use Wiki-cIE Code, REBEL-derived DPO data, and Wikipedia evaluation, including the existing entity-removal and negation scenarios. The added Appendix H.1 analysis explicitly reuses Section 5.3's Wikipedia data.

E2.justification: The SynthIE and ReLiK comparisons remain unchanged. Appendix H.1 adds numerical analysis of the constrained and unconstrained SynthIE modes already compared through examples in v1; it introduces no new comparison method.

E3.justification: Appendix H.1 adds quantitative error scoring for both SynthIE decoding modes using the existing Wikipedia sample and introduces an Entity/relation not in the KB category. Previously stated splits, training budgets, and benchmark evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v1's Appendix H.1 provided qualitative decoding examples; v2 retains them and adds a six-category quantitative error comparison in Table 4. The relation-frequency analysis, negation cases, and GPT-4o pipeline examples are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 95% confidence intervals constructed from 50 bootstrap samples. The additional error table extends the existing uncertainty-reporting practice, without changing reported run counts, seeds, or statistical estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3, Figure 2, and the existing appendix examples retain their results. New Table 4 reports additional error rates, including unconstrained SynthIE's unrelated-triplet fraction of 0.26 ± 0.11 and KB-violation fraction of 0.72 ± 0.11.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Appendix D metric definitions remain unchanged. The added Appendix H.1 evaluation is empirical and introduces no new theorem, proof, derivation, or formal assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and discussion retain the same BoostCD proposal, BoostIE application, and claims of improved in-distribution and out-of-distribution performance. The headline gains are unchanged; the new diagnostic supplies supporting evidence.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 newly explains that training on insufficiently exhaustive data could teach the base model to omit arbitrary triplets and reduce performance. Section 4 connects the KB-expressibility requirement to the choice of synthetic data. Existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix E newly identifies the trl library and supplies its documentation link for DPO finetuning. This is additional implementation disclosure; the stated hardware, hyperparameters, training times, and code access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography, related-work discussion, and positioning relative to earlier methods are unchanged. The added trl documentation link supplies implementation information without revising research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording and typo corrections, expands the training-data and Appendix H.1 explanations, adds cross-references, and updates author affiliations. The overall section organization and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 4 and corrects Figure 1's final relation label and color coding. Figure 3 moves from PDF page 13 to page 16, while the existing example Tables 4–6 become Tables 5–7. Other display changes mainly concern placement and spacing.

improvement.justification: The new Appendix H.1 table supplements v1's qualitative decoding examples with quantitative evidence about the two modes' different errors. Clearer training-data requirements, the corrected Figure 1, and disclosure of the DPO library improve clarity and reproducibility. These are useful but limited gains; the core method, benchmark results, and evaluation scale remain unchanged.
